b:
AIST Math Level 2 questions test conceptual fluency rather than rote execution. Success requires two disciplines:

  • Algebraic Rigor: Show complete intermediate steps for every equation; avoid unverified shortcuts.
  • Verification Check: Plug found roots back into original rational and logarithmic expressions to eliminate extraneous roots immediately.

f: Definition 1.1 — The imaginary unit and complex numbers
f_ar: Definition 1.1 — The imaginary unit and complex numbers
b: The imaginary unit \( i \) satisfies \( i^2=-1 \). A complex number is any expression \( z=a+bi \) with \( a,b\in\mathbb{R} \): \( a \) is the real part, written \( \operatorname{Re}(z) \), and \( b \) is the imaginary part, written \( \operatorname{Im}(z) \). When \( b=0 \), \( z \) is an ordinary real number; when \( a=0 \) and \( b\neq0 \), \( z \) is called purely imaginary.
b_ar: The imaginary unit \( i \) satisfies \( i^2=-1 \). When \( b=0 \), \( z \) is an ordinary real number; when \( a=0 \) and \( b\neq0 \), \( z \) is called purely imaginary.

b:
For \( z_1=a+bi \) and \( z_2=c+di \):

\[ z_1+z_2=(a+c)+(b+d)i \]

\[ z_1 z_2=(ac-bd)+(ad+bc)i \]

The multiplication rule is just FOIL followed by \( i^2\to -1 \): \( (a+bi)(c+di)=ac+adi+bci+bdi^2=(ac-bd)+(ad+bc)i \).

b: The complex conjugate of \( z=a+bi \) is \( \bar z=a-bi \) — same real part, opposite sign on the imaginary part. The modulus (or absolute value) of \( z \) is \[ |z|=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}, \] the distance from \( z \) to the origin when \( z \) is plotted as the point \( (a,b) \) in the complex plane.

b: For every complex number \( z=a+bi \), \[ z\bar z=|z|^2. \] In particular \( z\bar z \) is always a nonnegative real number.

f: Theorem 1.2 — De Moivre's Theorem for Powers
f_ar: مبرهنة 1.2 — De Moivre's مبرهنة for Powers
b:
For any complex number \( z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta) \) and any integer \( n \):

\[ z^n = \big[r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\big]^n = r^n \big(\cos(n\theta) + i\sin(n\theta)\big). \]
b_ar:
For any complex number \( z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta) \) and any integer \( n \):

\[ z^n = \big[r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\big]^n = r^n \big(\cos(n\theta) + i\sin(n\theta)\big). \]

f: Definition 2.1 — Matrix, addition, and scalar multiplication
f_ar: Definition 2.1 — Matrix, addition, and scalar multiplication
b:
An \( m\times n \) matrix is a rectangular array of numbers with \( m \) rows and \( n \) columns, written \( A=[a_{ij}] \) where \( a_{ij} \) is the entry in row \( i \), column \( j \). Two matrices of the same dimensions add entrywise, and a scalar \( k \) multiplies every entry:

\[ (A+B)_{ij}=a_{ij}+b_{ij}, \qquad (kA)_{ij}=k\,a_{ij}. \]
b_ar:
An \( m\times n \) matrix is a rectangular array of numbers with \( m \) rows and \( n \) columns, written \( A=[a_{ij}] \) where \( a_{ij} \) is the entry in row \( i \), column \( j \). Two matrices of the same dimensions add entrywise, and a scalar \( k \) multiplies every entry:

\[ (A+B)_{ij}=a_{ij}+b_{ij}, \qquad (kA)_{ij}=k\,a_{ij}. \]

b:
If \( A \) is \( m\times n \) and \( B \) is \( n\times p \) (the inner dimensions must match), the product \( AB \) is the \( m\times p \) matrix whose \( (i,j) \) entry is the dot product of row \( i \) of \( A \) with column \( j \) of \( B \):

\[ (AB)_{ij}=\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_{ik}b_{kj}. \]

Matrix multiplication is not commutative in general — \( AB\neq BA \) even when both products are defined.

f: Definition 2.3 — Determinant and the identity matrix
f_ar: تعريف 2.3 — المحدد and the المتطابقة المصفوفة
b: For a \( 2\times2 \) matrix \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \), the determinant is the scalar \[ \det A=ad-bc. \] The \( 2\times2 \) identity matrix \( I=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix} \) satisfies \( IA=AI=A \) for every \( 2\times2 \) matrix \( A \) — it's the multiplicative identity.
b_ar: For a \( 2\times2 \) matrix \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \), the determinant is the scalar \[ \det A=ad-bc. \] The \( 2\times2 \) identity matrix \( I=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix} \) satisfies \( IA=AI=A \) for every \( 2\times2 \) matrix \( A \) — it's the multiplicative identity.

b:
If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \det A=ad-bc\neq0 \), then \( A \) is invertible, with

\[ A^{-1}=\frac{1}{\det A}\begin{bmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{bmatrix}. \]

If \( \det A=0 \), no inverse exists.
b_ar:

f: Definition 2.4 — Vectors: magnitude and dot product
f_ar: تعريف 2.4 — المتجهات: magnitude and dot product
b: A vector \( \mathbf{u}=\langle u_1,u_2\rangle \) in the plane has magnitude \( |\mathbf{u}|=\sqrt{u_1^2+u_2^2} \). The dot product of \( \mathbf{u}=\langle u_1,u_2\rangle \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\langle v_1,v_2\rangle \) is the scalar \[ \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=u_1v_1+u_2v_2. \]
b_ar: A vector \( \mathbf{u}=\langle u_1,u_2\rangle \) in the plane has magnitude \( |\mathbf{u}|=\sqrt{u_1^2+u_2^2} \). The dot product of \( \mathbf{u}=\langle u_1,u_2\rangle \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\langle v_1,v_2\rangle \) is the scalar \[ \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=u_1v_1+u_2v_2. \]

b: For nonzero vectors \( \mathbf{u},\mathbf{v} \) with angle \( \theta \) between them, \[ \cos\theta=\frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}|\,|\mathbf{v}|}. \]

A sequence \( a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots \) is arithmetic if consecutive terms differ by a constant \( d \), the common difference: \( a_{n+1}=a_n+d \). Its explicit (closed-form) formula is

\[ a_n=a_1+(n-1)d. \]
b_ar:
A sequence \( a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots \) is arithmetic if consecutive terms differ by a constant \( d \), the common difference: \( a_{n+1}=a_n+d \). Its explicit (closed-form) formula is

b:
An arithmetic series is the sum of an arithmetic sequence's first \( n \) terms. Pairing the first term with the last, the second with the second-to-last, and so on (each pair sums to \( a_1+a_n \)) gives

\[ S_n=\frac{n}{2}\big(a_1+a_n\big)=\frac{n}{2}\big(2a_1+(n-1)d\big). \]

b:
A sequence is geometric if consecutive terms share a constant ratio \( r\neq0 \): \( a_{n+1}=r\,a_n \). Its explicit formula is

\[ a_n=a_1\,r^{\,n-1}. \]

b:
For \( r\neq1 \), the sum of the first \( n \) terms of a geometric sequence is

\[ S_n=\frac{a_1(r^n-1)}{r-1}. \]

If \( |r|<1 \), the infinite geometric series \( a_1+a_1r+a_1r^2+\cdot s \) converges to

\[ S_\infty=\frac{a_1}{1-r}. \] If \( |r|\geq1 \) (and \( a_1\neq0 \)), the series diverges — it has no finite sum.

b: The composition of \( f \) and \( g \), written \( (f\circ g)(x) \) or \( f(g(x)) \), means: apply \( g \) first, then apply \( f \) to the result. In general \( f(g(x))\neq g(f(x)) \) — order matters.

b: A function \( f \) is one-to-one if it never sends two different inputs to the same output. Only one-to-one functions have an inverse \( f^{-1} \), the function that undoes \( f \): \[ f\big(f^{-1}(x)\big)=x \quad\text{and}\quad f^{-1}\big(f(x)\big)=x. \] To find \( f^{-1} \) algebraically: write \( y=f(x) \), swap \( x \) and \( y \), then solve for \( y \).

Only one-to-one functions have an inverse \( f^{-1} \), the function that undoes \( f \): \[ f\big(f^{-1}(x)\big)=x \quad\text{and}\quad f^{-1}\big(f(x)\big)=x. \] To find \( f^{-1} \) algebraically: write \( y=f(x) \), swap \( x \) and \( y \), then solve for \( y \).

b: A rational equation has a variable in a denominator. Solve by clearing denominators (multiply both sides by them), then solve the resulting polynomial equation — but always check each solution in the original equation, since a value that makes a denominator zero is an extraneous solution and must be rejected even if it satisfies the cleared version.

b: An exponential equation has the variable in an exponent; solve by matching bases (\( b^{m}=b^{n}\Rightarrow m=n \)) when possible. A logarithmic equation has the variable inside a log; the key identity is \( \log_b x+\log_b y=\log_b(xy) \), and every solution must be checked against the log's domain (\( x>0 \)).

In any triangle with angles \( A,B,C \) and opposite sides \( a,b,c \):

\[ \frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}. \]

Use it when you know an angle-side pair plus one more angle or side.

b:
In any triangle, with \( C \) the angle between sides \( a \) and \( b \) (opposite side \( c \)):

\[ c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C. \]

Use it when you know two sides and the included angle (SAS), or all three sides (SSS, solving for an angle).

A point's polar coordinates \( (r,\theta) \) give its distance \( r \) from the origin and the angle \( \theta \) (measured counterclockwise from the positive \( x \)-axis). Converting between polar and rectangular \( (x,y) \):

\[ x=r\cos\theta,\quad y=r\sin\theta, \qquad r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2},\quad \tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}\ (x\neq0). \]

b: We write \[ \lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L \] to mean: as \( x \) approaches \( a \) (from either side, without necessarily equaling \( a \)), \( f(x) \) approaches \( L \). When \( f \) is a polynomial or rational function and \( a \) is in its domain, the limit is found simply by direct substitution: \( \lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a) \).
